\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA) across six models spanning three architecture families across three reasoning domains (FOLIO, ProofWriter, LogiQA), and over 3,000 evaluation instances with four-seed replication on the primary condition. Grounded in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, our analysis explains why Self-Consistency majority voting saturates and why symbolic constraint aggregation fails to break this plateau under same-model self-extraction.

The central finding is the independence bottleneck. Same-model traces produce Fleiss' $\kappa$ values of $0.21$--$0.82$ among instruction-tuned models (0.91 for thinking mode), and the effective sample size compresses to Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ at $K = 12$. Self-extracted FOL constraints inherit this correlation structure. We observe a narrow favorable region around 50--55\% SC accuracy in one model-dataset condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO): Mistral-7B on FOLIO shows a positive directional trend of $+3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$, 2 of 4 seeds marginal at $p < 0.10$, none reaching $p < 0.05$; 4-seed mean $+1.47$\,pp). Outside this zone, confirmation bias renders constraints non-discriminative (Type~A) or error amplification actively degrades accuracy by $-2.83$\,pp (Type~C).

Oracle controls confirm that the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling. \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments provide a causal identification of the failure source.
Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only the constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$; \S\ref{sec:oracle}).
The best self-extraction result across all models and conditions captures only 24.1\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling.
Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap between oracle and self-extracted performance localizes entirely to extraction quality, not to solver limitations or the MAX-SAT formulation.
The aggregation mechanism is sound; the constraints are not.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The direct channel limits voting diversity: the Condorcet Jury Theorem predicts that aggregation improves accuracy only when voters contribute independent information \citep{condorcet1785, ladha1992correlated}, and Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate this requirement at $K = 12$. This channel explains the SC plateau. The indirect channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, yielding a discriminative rate of only 8.2\% (\S\ref{sec:extraction-taxonomy}) and causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to weighted vote counting (\S\ref{sec:ablation}). This channel explains why SICA fails to surpass SC. The oracle result disambiguates the two: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that channel (b) is the proximal bottleneck. Trace correlation is the root cause, but its effect on SICA is mediated primarily through constraint homogenization rather than through voting diversity alone.

The extraction step maps natural language traces to FOL through the same model distribution, so constraints inherit the correlation structure of the traces that produced them.
Even symbolic representations, which appear to introduce a qualitatively different signal (formal logic rather than natural language votes), collapse back into the shared model distribution once the extraction is performed by the same model.
The independence bottleneck is not about symbolic reasoning as a formalism; it is about self-extraction being unable to introduce information that the model does not already encode in its traces.

Nine interventions spanning six dimensions all fail to widen the favorable region (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
Contrastive prompting reduces the non-discriminative rate from 8.2\% to 6.0\%, but the newly discriminative constraints still mirror model bias.
Cross-model extraction fails in both directions: a weaker model extracting from stronger traces yields 0\% discriminative constraints, while stronger models (14B+) extracting from weaker traces (7B) produce accuracy within $\pm$1\,pp of self-extraction.
Only 1 of 4 temperature settings produces a positive SICA effect; $T = 0.3$, $0.5$, and $1.0$ all yield negative or null effects ($\Delta \in [-1.47, 0.00]$\,pp).
Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break the confirmation bias pattern.
The consistent failure across orthogonal intervention strategies constitutes the strongest evidence that the bottleneck is structural, not an artifact of prompt design or solver configuration.
If any single dimension had succeeded, the bottleneck could be attributed to engineering; the uniform failure across all six implicates the self-extraction paradigm itself.

Published systems that report positive results on logical reasoning each bypass same-model self-extraction.
DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos} composes specialized solvers, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle} applies logic-complete decomposition, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover} trains dedicated FOL verifiers, and Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm} routes problems to external provers.
Our oracle result is consistent with their success: when constraints are discriminative (by whatever mechanism), symbolic aggregation works.
The critical difference is the source of constraints, not the aggregation procedure.
These systems trade the simplicity of self-extraction for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal, exactly the property that CJT requires \citep{ladha1992correlated}.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches statistical significance at $\alpha = 0.05$. The four-seed replication of Mistral-7B on FOLIO yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$; 2 of 4 seeds show marginal positive trends ($p < 0.10$) but none survives any correction for multiple comparisons. Effects range from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp (4-seed mean $+1.47$\,pp). We report these as directional evidence, not significance claims. In contrast, the negative effects are significant: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$) both reach $p < 0.05$, confirming that error amplification in the Type~C regime is a reliable phenomenon. \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments provide a causal identification of the failure source.
Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only the constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$; \S\ref{sec:oracle}).
The best self-extraction result across all models and conditions captures only 24.1\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling.
Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap between oracle and self-extracted performance localizes entirely to extraction quality, not to solver limitations or the MAX-SAT formulation.
The aggregation mechanism is sound; the constraints are not.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The direct channel limits voting diversity: the Condorcet Jury Theorem predicts that aggregation improves accuracy only when voters contribute independent information \citep{condorcet1785, ladha1992correlated}, and Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate this requirement at $K = 12$. This channel explains the SC plateau. The indirect channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, yielding a discriminative rate of only 8.2\% (\S\ref{sec:extraction-taxonomy}) and causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to weighted vote counting (\S\ref{sec:ablation}). This channel explains why SICA fails to surpass SC. The oracle result disambiguates the two: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that channel (b) is the proximal bottleneck. Trace correlation is the root cause, but its effect on SICA is mediated primarily through constraint homogenization rather than through voting diversity alone.

The extraction step maps natural language traces to FOL through the same model distribution, so constraints inherit the correlation structure of the traces that produced them.
Even symbolic representations, which appear to introduce a qualitatively different signal (formal logic rather than natural language votes), collapse back into the shared model distribution once the extraction is performed by the same model.
The independence bottleneck is not about symbolic reasoning as a formalism; it is about self-extraction being unable to introduce information that the model does not already encode in its traces.

Nine interventions spanning six dimensions all fail to widen the intermediate-SC region (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
Contrastive prompting reduces the non-discriminative rate from 8.2\% to 6.0\%, but the newly discriminative constraints still mirror model bias.
Cross-model extraction fails in both directions: a weaker model extracting from stronger traces yields 0\% discriminative constraints, while stronger models (14B+) extracting from weaker traces (7B) produce accuracy within $\pm$1\,pp of self-extraction.
Only 1 of 4 temperature settings produces a positive SICA effect; $T = 0.3$, $0.5$, and $1.0$ all yield negative or null effects ($\Delta \in [-1.47, 0.00]$\,pp).
Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break the confirmation bias pattern.
The consistent failure across orthogonal intervention strategies constitutes the strongest evidence that the bottleneck is structural, not an artifact of prompt design or solver configuration.
If any single dimension had succeeded, the bottleneck could be attributed to engineering; the uniform failure across all six implicates the self-extraction paradigm itself.

Published systems that report positive results on logical reasoning each bypass same-model self-extraction.
DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos} composes specialized solvers, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle} applies logic-complete decomposition, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover} trains dedicated FOL verifiers, and Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm} routes problems to external provers.
Our oracle result is consistent with their success: when constraints are discriminative (by whatever mechanism), symbolic aggregation works.
The critical difference is the source of constraints, not the aggregation procedure.
These systems trade the simplicity of self-extraction for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal, exactly the property that CJT requires \citep{ladha1992correlated}.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches statistical significance at $\alpha = 0.05$. The four-seed replication of Mistral-7B on FOLIO yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$; 2 of 4 seeds show marginal positive trends ($p < 0.10$) but none survives any correction for multiple comparisons. Effects range from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp (4-seed mean $+1.47$\,pp). We report these as directional evidence, not significance claims. In contrast, the negative effects are significant: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$) both reach $p < 0.05$, confirming that error amplification in the Type~C regime is a reliable phenomenon. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$ on two datasets). The converging evidence for the independence bottleneck does not rest on any single $p$-value but on the pattern across analyses: positive direction in only 2/4 seeds, cross-model entropy decomposition showing regime-dependent mechanism (\S\ref{sec:entropy}), discriminative rate CI of [7.6, 8.8]\%, and the oracle-extraction gap.

For practitioners, $C_0$ (multi-candidate rate) combined with SC accuracy forms a zero-cost deployment diagnostic before any constraint extraction is attempted.
When $C_0 < 5\%$, SICA reduces to SC by construction (degenerate).
When SC exceeds ${\sim}60\%$, confirmation bias renders constraints non-discriminative (Type~A).
When SC falls below ${\sim}40\%$, error amplification makes constraints actively harmful (Type~C).
Only a narrow band around 50--55\% SC in one model-dataset condition shows positive effects, and even there, self-extraction captures barely a quarter of the oracle ceiling.
Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence, as CJT predicts is necessary: trained extractors (data-driven), external provers (tool-augmented), and multi-model pipelines (ensemble-based).
Each introduces a constraint source that is not a deterministic function of the reasoning model's own distribution.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA) across six models spanning three architecture families across three reasoning domains (FOLIO, ProofWriter, LogiQA), and over 3,000 evaluation instances with four-seed replication on the primary condition. Grounded in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, our analysis explains why Self-Consistency majority voting saturates and why symbolic constraint aggregation fails to break this plateau under same-model self-extraction.

The central finding is the independence bottleneck. Same-model traces produce Fleiss' $\kappa$ values of $0.21$--$0.82$ among instruction-tuned models (0.91 for thinking mode), and the effective sample size compresses to Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ at $K = 12$. Self-extracted FOL constraints inherit this correlation structure. We observe an intermediate-SC region around 50--55\% accuracy in one model-dataset condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO): Mistral-7B on FOLIO shows a positive directional trend of $+3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$, 2 of 4 seeds marginal at $p < 0.10$, none reaching $p < 0.05$; 4-seed mean $+1.47$\,pp). Outside this zone, confirmation bias renders constraints non-discriminative (Type~A) or error amplification actively degrades accuracy by $-2.83$\,pp (Type~C).

Oracle controls confirm that the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling. Nine remediation strategies spanning six intervention dimensions all fail to widen the effective zone. The uniform failure confirms the bottleneck is structural rather than an engineering artifact. Sensitivity analysis reinforces this conclusion: $K = 12$ is the only setting with $\Delta > 2$\,pp among five $K$ values, and only 1 of 4 temperature settings ($T = 0.7$) produces a positive effect; both peaks coincide with a relatively low SC baseline.

The multi-candidate rate $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic for predicting when symbolic aggregation can help. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence as CJT requires: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\paragraph{Limitations.} Our evaluation covers same-model self-extraction and cross-model extraction in both directions (\S\ref{sec:remediation}), but we do not test trained FOL extractors or external solvers with verified grounding, which may overcome the independence bottleneck. The intermediate-SC region where positive trends occur is narrow (SC $\approx$ 50--55\%) and observed in only one model-dataset condition, limiting practical applicability. The optimal $K$ and temperature settings cannot be determined without labeled data, as both sensitivity analyses show the best configuration coincides with the lowest SC baseline rather than following a predictable trend. Our evaluation covers formal reasoning benchmarks (FOLIO, ProofWriter, LogiQA) but lacks open-domain validation where formalizability is lower and failure modes may differ. Finally, four-seed replication on the primary condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO) shows effects ranging from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp, with 2 of 4 seeds yielding null or negative results, indicating that even the most promising condition produces unreliable improvements.
